Note::url_encode¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::url_encode() const

Percent-Encode Every Cell For Use In A URL¶

url_encode() returns a new Note, same shape as the input, with each cell percent-encoded so it can be dropped into a URL path segment or query value without changing the URL’s structure. Use it when building request URLs, ?key=value pairs, or redirect targets from text that may contain spaces, &, =, /, ?, #, or non-ASCII characters.

The rule¶

The unreserved set of RFC 3986 is left as-is:

A-Z   a-z   0-9   -   _   .   ~

Every other byte is written as % followed by its two uppercase hex digits. This means:

  • A space becomes %20 (not + — this is component encoding, not application/x-www-form-urlencoded).

  • The sub-delimiters and gen-delimiters & = / ? # : @ [ ] and so on are all encoded, so an encoded value cannot break out of its path segment or query field.

  • Non-ASCII text is encoded per UTF-8 byte: é (bytes C3 A9) becomes %C3%A9, and € (bytes E2 82 AC) becomes %E2%82%AC.

url_decode() is the exact inverse.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Encoded cells are longer wherever a byte had to be escaped; an empty cell stays empty.

Example 1: Reserved Characters And Spaces¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"a b&c=d", "path/to/x?y#z"}).url_encode())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["a%20b%26c%3Dd", "path%2Fto%2Fx%3Fy%23z"]

Space → %20, & → %26, = → %3D, / → %2F, ? → %3F, # → %23.

Example 2: Unreserved Characters Pass Through¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::make_note({"A-Za-z0-9-_.~"}).url_encode();
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["A-Za-z0-9-_.~"]

Example 3: Non-ASCII Is Encoded Per UTF-8 Byte¶

pluss::note::print(std::cout,
                   pluss::make_note({"café", "€"}).url_encode())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["caf%C3%A9", "%E2%82%AC"]

Example 4: Round-Trips Through url_decode¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::make_note({"a b/c?d", "café"}).url_encode().url_decode())
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["a b/c?d", "café"]

  • pluss::coden::Note::url_decode: the inverse.

  • Note::base64_encode: the other “make it ASCII-safe” encoding, for transfer rather than URL syntax.
